findings.failure_path: A base such as CCL_SKILL_BASE_REF=--quiet is passed to git diff before the -- separator and is parsed as a Git option, not a revision. In a clean PR checkout Git then compares the index with the working tree, reports no paths, and the gate exits successfully with “no reviewed-path change” despite committed changes relative to the real base. This also violates the requirement that an unresolvable base be reported unevaluated.
findings.smallest_fix: Resolve the supplied base to a commit with git rev-parse --verify --end-of-options before any diff; reject or report unevaluated when resolution fails, and pass only the resolved commit hash to both changed_skill_paths and freeze_packet.

findings.failure_path: Succession establishes terminality solely from autonomous_review_index == challenge_budget + 1. A caller can provide a tracked challenge receipt with budget 1 and index 2 but challenge_index=0, autonomous_reviews_remaining=1, autonomous_review_allowed=true, or an empty prior-result prefix. The controller accepts it and mints the succeeding challenge even though the predecessor is not a coherent terminal chain receipt, bypassing the bounded autonomous-round transition.
findings.smallest_fix: Validate all terminal receipt arithmetic before accepting succession: challenge_index equals the budget, autonomous_review_budget equals budget + 1, remaining is zero, autonomous_review_allowed is false, the prior-result prefix has the required length, and the challenge focus is non-empty; also reject reuse of the predecessor chain ID.

skipped_clients.reason: claude belongs to the implementer model family

concern_results.conclusion: Two bypasses remain: option-shaped base values can produce a false-green merge check, and succession accepts receipts whose terminal-round fields are internally inconsistent.
The autonomous-review boundary is not contained because the controller can authorize a succession from a receipt that does not prove the predecessor chain actually spent its budget.
